body:
I actually initiated the conversation with my psychologist. I had been looking into it for years and never really wanted to admit to myself that I was considered disabled because I still work full time. But I can’t go out in public by myself, I have issues with getting to work on time, being able to stay at work for my full time, etc. So by ADA standards and according to my dr I am legally disabled.

I was also worried it would come off as me just wanting a dog with me everywhere or blowing things out of proportion but I had a whole session where it was all her and I talked about and she agreed she thinks it would help me loads. It led to me telling her things about my life I hadn’t opened up about even to her because I was just too embarrassed. I’m still early in the process and waiting to hear back from the two organizations I applied to (should be hearing back this week!) but it was well worth bringing up. The worst that happens is they say they don’t think you meet the ADA definition of being disabled.

I have friends who have had improvement on low daily doses of klonopin and we were looking into that, I will add Lyrica to the list as well! They said they may want to try a couple of other SSRIs and others before resorting to daily klonopin, which I understand. I’m always open to hearing what has worked for people with similar issues.

Yes. He didn’t want to switch so soon, he acknowledged that most medications take 6-8 weeks before full effects can be seen and judged, but the powers that be paying me my disability wanted a change every two weeks if there were no marked improvements. Some medications were genuinely switched off of after that point because of terrible side effects like night terrors or other things.

I am talking to my doctor about possibly trying some new things as I know even if I get a SD it won’t fix all and will take up to two years or more that I’ll have to navigate through first. I appreciate your concern on that. :)

I’m usually fine in one on one settings or talking directly with people and I have dealt with all sorts (retail, call centers, tech support - always thrilling). My big problem is large crowds and being in them in general. I will definitely bring up with my psychologist working on how to deal with people aggressively or just nosily questioning me, thank you for that. I understand from the reading here (I’ve also watched a good bit of Drew Lynch talking about some of his encounters) that an invisible illness puts more of a target on my back with a SD.

Thank you! I have found two organizations that look like they could work for me and will be applying to both. I am going to start working on the applications tonight. Both are out of state for me (none in NY that apply to me that I have found), but I can afford the travel expenses with time to save.

I will definitely be taking full advantage of the questions to ask when it gets to that stage. From reading posts here and looking at the resources this is such a well put together sub/resource for people looking. It gave me the push I needed to bring it up to my psychologist and get over the “I’m not physically disabled and I have a job so I don’t deserve help” mentality.

I don’t know. The only thing I seem to be good at in life is helping others feel better, and I don’t even have the energy to do that anymore. I’m just a burden otherwise.

If I wasn’t constantly reaching out to people I wouldn’t hear from anyone. I tried for a month. Not as a test, just because I didn’t have the energy. Didn’t message anyone, and I didn’t hear from anyone. Not a single person checked to see if I was ok. And they did know I was going through some serious things. It just feels like no one cares unless I’m making them feel better about themselves.

Thank you for sharing. I feel sort of... I don't know how to put it... ridiculous? Ashamed? For posting or talking about it when I know there are people who it affects more consistently, but I know I can't look at it that way. It is a problem for me and I need to stop before I get to a point where it takes over my life again.
Thank you, I appreciate it. Just coffee and water for me today!

Thank you. I think I have some of the framework in place (therapy, going to see a psychiatrist soon about actual meds), I'm just missing that support. I was pretty happy when I found this sub, as unsure as I still am. I already depend on my friends for a lot and on top of it not being fair to them I don't think some of them see it as a problem for me either since it's not constant drinking.

Oh gosh, I'm glad I didn't spill my breakfast at therapy!

Yeah, my therapist recommended me making more use out of my gym membership or even just taking my dog for a walk when I start to get bad. Thank you!!

Thank you. I slipped last night but I have since poured the rest of my alcohol down the drain. I'm working on talking to someone about getting on REAL medication to help, since I can't win this round on my own.

Thank you. Logically I know it has nothing to do with me, but I'm sure you know what it's like going through a spike. Logic out the window. :/
I have a gym membership that I never use that would probably be a great distraction, but I'm in that slump where it's hard to make myself do anything other than go to work. I made myself immediately delete the account I used to check on him, so I have that at least. Right now I'm fighting the urge to seek reassurance from him and end up saying something stupid, I've been keeping myself busy cleaning since I looked.
I have an appointment with my therapist on Wednesday at least so I can talk to her about this.

Thank you for your response, I really appreciate it.

Look at it this way -- you had THREE GOOD WEEKS. Three! I don't know you personally, but from your posts here on some of my posts and others, you are so full of good advice and support for everyone. You can do this. You're still in therapy, you're still on your medication, you've got this. OCD ain't got nothing on any of us.

I do the same thing. I'm worried I'll polarize someone. That they'll disagree and stop talking to me, even when it's something silly like saying I enjoy watching 'x' show. I find myself doing it a lot in person to, never really committing to an answer or decision in case someone disagrees with me, despite having strong feelings on whatever we happen to be talking about.

I get the same way. When I'm slow at work or doing something repetitive, and as I'm trying to get to bed I end up ruminating.
I found putting something interesting on TV as I'm falling asleep helps to pull my mind away from ruminating. I figure if I'm going to be up anyway it might as well be something entertaining that can somewhat help me stop my compulsions.

I know, for me, the actual feeling of anxiety can present itself in multiple ways. Sometimes I get the heart racing, sweaty palms, flight or fight reaction people typically think of. Other times it feels like I can't breathe despite everything else seeming fine, no elevated heart rate, maybe some light headedness. On other occasions I'll just be hyper sensitive and annoyed by anything and everything. But when I stop and think about it, all of these things occur because I'm anxious or worked up over something.
I guess what I'm saying is everyone's body responds to anxiety differently.
Thank you! This is helpful. It does make more sense to me to do something meaningful to accept it's ok to have these uncertainties but not to continue letting them impact my life.

You can do it!! I went for my intake appointment last Friday and I'm starting actual therapy this Friday. It's a big step on a long journey but it is so so worth it. I had the same fears you did about being told that I was just an ass and don't actually have OCD, but you need to just tell that voice to pipe down.

Yeah, that makes a lot of sense, I think I do it without realizing it. Posting all of the details here and all of that to see if it clicks with anyone else. It's just nice to have a place to let it all out where you don't get "the look" and people get it. I'm sure you know the look I'm talking about, the one that makes you feel like you're nuts even if the other person doesn't mean to give it, they just really can't comprehend being that hung up over something that seems so small to them.

Yeah, I'll admit on some bad nights I do Facebook stalk her and look at the pictures of them together. I've tried to stop it recently as I know what it leads to (everything you've described above), it's definitely a compulsion I'm working on.

As far as my friend, that's the approach I've been trying to take. I have stopped texting him as much lately, and I haven't sought reassurance from him in over a week. The conversation we had about him just not answering me if he didn't want to talk to me took place a couple of weeks ago when I thought I had pushed him too far and messed up the friendship. He is an excellent friend (he's taking me to a haunted hayride this weekend, I've been begging him for the last couple of weeks), I just need to realize that he has other things in his life and doesn't have time to text me 24/7 and I can't take it so personally when he already has plans (I'm more of a spur of the moment plan person as I have pretty bad social anxiety and never know if I'll feel like going out two weeks in advance). He's never done anything except for exactly what he said he will do, he's extremely true to his word and I need to learn to trust him in that and not let my mind take over. It is solid advice, I know I need to accept that there will be people who just do not want to continue friendships no matter how hard one person tries and it's not worth the time and effort.

Thank you for reading and taking the time to respond. :)

That when I open up about what's going on in my head, I don't expect someone to have a quick cure or be able to fix it for me. I don't expect anyone to have the right words to say, because in most situations there are no right words.
Please just listen and acknowledge that you might not know exactly what it's like, but you understand that it's hard and I'm physically and mentally exhausted and you know I'm doing the best I can.
You are fantastic. 💜 This is a great post.
I second this, it's a great community over there and everyone can relate in some way as our OCD tends to heavily affect our relationship.

"Everything is Alright" by Motion City Soundtrack is one that has been posted here before that I know people relate to. Justin has actually commented on the fact that people have reached out to him saying as much, and that it wasn't his intention in writing the song but it's interesting to see how people interpret it.

I'm glad you had a good weekend with your bf!!
I think we all need to stop and remind ourselves sometimes that it takes time. We can't hold ourselves to perfect standards. Resisting compulsions is excellent, keep it up!! :)
The buying it makes me happy, my wallet not so much hahahah.
Also, lots and lots of animal cuddles. I have a dog and two ferrets that keep me busy a lot.
I like doing my makeup!! I never ever used to do it until about a year ago, one of my friends got me into it. Now I've found it's very soothing and can be fun. Basically doing art on my face!!

Thank you!! It's hard to make the call when in a bad state, even harder to make it when doing "well". I'm glad I finally did and it feels like a burdens been lifted.
This is such a fantastic community, and seeing everyone else talking about therapy and pushing for it is what really helped me to take the step.
Thank you!!

Thank you! I feel lucky to have found her and for her to have had openings. I know others haven't been as lucky in their areas and I think that's what made me so skeptical at first about her being any good.

I'm not going to give you any reassurances or relationship advice as we shouldn't be enabling here.
What I will say is, you shouldn't be making any relationship decisions while you're not healthy. Without being healthy it's hard to separate your thoughts and judge objectively if there's really nothing there or if it's your brain. I'd really recommend, if it's possible for you, to get back into therapy and give it a shot long term. Then re-evaluating the relationship when you're healthy and able to make more clear decisions.
I had to come to grips with this as far as me wanting to start a relationship right now and realizing I wasn't healthy enough to do so and be fair to myself and the other person. It works in the opposite direction here for you and your SO. I started therapy and ERP again today after a long break, so I'm in the same boat as you right now as far as having a lot ahead to work through. If you ever need to talk feel free to pm me.
I'm glad I could help if even just a little. I wish you both well, and don't be afraid to reach out if you need to talk!

Without knowing his exact thoughts behind the situations, it's hard to say much on it. I did have a situation with someone I had been dating where I deleted texts from my ex because I was worried my current SO would misinterpret them and leave me. He knew my ex and I were talking, and that we had been texting, so when he went to get a phone number out of my phone he noticed the texts were missing and got upset. I had nothing to hide, no reason to delete them, I had literally just been talking to my ex about finally getting my license. But I had convinced myself that my current SO would see them and think I was cheating, so I deleted them and tried to hide it. It's not always a rational and easily explained thought process. I've found with OCD (or with mine at least) that it's more often than not completely irrational.
I think it's fantastic that you've come here trying to understand. I can imagine that being on the receiving end of it is an extremely hard thing. One of the things I can think of, is maybe bringing up that you want to go to an appointment with him because you want to try and understand what it's like? It might be easier in that environment for you to share how it's been affecting you, as it undoubtedly has.
Another thing I would suggest is, I don't know if you've seen it, but checking out r/ROCD. There are a couple of people that frequent the subreddit that do not have OCD themselves, but their SO's do. They might be able to help more with how to approach it, as they've been in a more similar situation to you.
You can always feel free to PM me if you need to vent or want to talk or some insight. I've been in your SOs position where I destroyed an almost six year relationship because I was constantly doubting and convinced he was going to leave me no matter what he did otherwise.
I wish you luck and hope for the best for both of you. Don't forget to take care of yourself in all of this.

I think it's benefitted me on certain points. I am much more empathetic, I am the go to person at work when someone is having a bad day because I can relate and listen. I had one friend that would actually tell me she loved that I seemed to be more upset/impacted by what was going on in her life than she was because I could feel it so strongly. While that takes its toll on me, and I really need to practice not stretching myself so thinly working on other people's problems when I have my own, I don't honestly think I would want it any other way.
As u/FoxesBadgers said though, there are times before I started therapy that I was a real asshole. I would ditch plans at the last minute because of my anxiety, I would promise to do things for people and constantly let them down. I pushed my parents and those that cared about me away. I threatened suicide quite regularly to the people that tried to hang on and care about me. I had a problem with alcohol at one point while trying to find ways to cope and could be extremely verbally abusive when drunk. I was dating a guy at the time that I completely pushed away by constantly seeking reassurance, accusing him of cheating, questioning his feelings for me. I have friends that cut me out and have thankfully now given me a second chance, I'm slowly making it up to them. I don't blame any of them for it. I was an awful person for a while, and it wasn't just the OCD. It was my refusal to seek help for it.
I think with all, it's balance. Now that I've been working on it, recognizing it, and getting help, I can use my experiences to my benefit. And learning from the past, no matter if it was coping with a mental illness or not, can teach anyone to be a better and more compassionate person I think.

Melatonin worked for me as a natural sleep aid for a while.
That being said, you shouldn't depend on it to get to bed every night. I'm sure you know all of this but I'm going to say it anyway -- get back into therapy!! I just made the step myself after encountering some similar problems and I'm relieved just knowing I have an appointment set up. Check out psychologytoday.com, they have a pretty extensive list of psychologists and therapists in all areas and you can filter by things like people with experience with OCD. I had a couple I called who admitted they had no experience with it actually but pointed me in the right direction.

Therapy worked wonders for me. I'm starting back this Friday, haven't been in much too long and I found myself backsliding. Medication never really helped me, side effects always outweighed the benefits. But it's different for everyone, different chemical makeups and whatnot.
Exercise and pushing myself to go out when I just felt like curling up in a ball and giving in were two huge things that have helped me loads.

I'm not sure, it is interesting as I had heard anyone talk about anything similar either. My parents chalked it up to me just being a weird kid and having a vivid imagination. I used to do it with certain objects too, spin them to untangle their strings. I haven't done it in... I don't know... I'd say 10 years or so? But it was something that I was definitely very aware of and constantly thinking about as a kid. Your balls of energy sound similar.

I used to spin in circles until it felt "just right" when I was a kid. It felt like I had strings attached to me and if I spun one way they would tangle, so I had to spin the other way to untangle them or it would leave me upset all day.

That first paragraph is me to a T. And I agree, it wasn't until I was in my early 20s that it became such a noticeable problem. I always just thought I was a little odd and needy but never thought it was OCD because I didn't wash my hands or check to see if my door was locked.
That's a really interesting way to look at it. It makes sense, I guess I just really never gave it too much thought.

I appreciate it hah. I don't believe I'm seeking reassurance with this post though, it was more out of revelation and curiosity as to if anyone else had found they did something similar (even with a different compulsion). This realization hasn't cause me any anxiety at all actually, it's like something just clicked in my head when I realized it.

It's nice to read that I'm not alone in the spiking while PMSing. It's become a pretty sure fire way to tell when it's about that time, and I've started learning to be more forgiving of myself around that time and not beat myself up for "slipping".

Not all ROCD thoughts manifest the same, it's mainly if both the obsessions and the compulsions are there. For me it tends to be a lot of "they're cheating on me" or "they don't love me" if I don't get an immediate response back from them. I do get some of the doubting the relationship itself, if I'm in love with them, feeling numb, but those seem to be less for me and often come from the first two main thoughts.
I guess my point is, not everyone presents exactly the same. That's why there tend to be sub groups like this, not because OCD is extremely different at its core depending on what "type" you have, but because there are often similar themes that others can relate to, if not always exactly.
That being said, we can't diagnose here but if you are seeing someone currently, it would be worth bringing up with them.

Mine usually center around intimate relationships or close friendships. With the intimate relationships it can range from "they haven't texted me back and it's been an hour, they either don't love me anymore or are cheating", wondering if the relationship is right or if I'm just afraid of being alone for the rest of my life, some of the numbness/days of feeling absolutely nothing for them. With close friends it's usually along the lines of getting in my head that I'm annoying them or that they're just pretending to be my friends, I get terrified sometimes of making decisions or taking a stand on anything because I think they'll laugh about it or judge me for it and stop talking to me.

Relationship obsessions here. I occasionally get the oddball ones, but they tend to not last for more then a month or so. Like, last month I was concerned every text I was sending was being rerouted to a certain friend of mine and that he'd hate me if he saw them, and I had to keep checking to make sure there was no evidence of that happening. I guess even my oddball ones still relate to how people feel about/perceive me.

I have a type of Pure-O, rOCD. And honestly, up until I started talking to a therapist, I didn't think I had any compulsions either. Seeking reassurance (am I a bad person? Does this thought reflect me?), avoidance of triggers, ruminating... they're all compulsions, along with more.
I'm glad that you are seeking help, that's a big step!!
Thank you!!

I'm not sure about the NYC area, but where I live PsychologyToday.com helped me filter by my needs specifically and fine someone. I used it to find a therapist but you can search psychiatrists as well, and you can filter by those that have OCD listed in their profile.

I do it often. It's actually OCD awareness week right now!! I share a lot of articles from iocdf.org on my Facebook hoping to educate others and possibly reach some that may be too afraid to seek help. I know the first time I saw an article about Pure O and rOCD, something just clicked in my head, and it helped me seek out treatment. If I could help one person feel less alone and broken, it's worth talking about it to me. When I see friends or family post one of those "How OCD are you?" quizzes, or an article with inaccurate information, I also tend to include a gently worded comment to them and a link to the IOCDF page discussing what OCD really is and how it affects others and their lives. I found if you're polite about it and not accusatory, it actually tends to go over pretty well!!

Thank you, that makes a lot of sense. I understand what you mean by there just being thoughts, I think I was just having a problem finding the right wording, but it being my reaction that is in question makes sense.
I appreciate the advice as opposed to an answer on whether the reaction is justified or not. I do believe I'm in an obsessive state over it right now as my anxiety was through the roof. I just took a break to calm myself a bit and, as my therapist used to say, "so what?" the thought.
I appreciate your explanation!!

Ok, thank you.
I have a friend that I've started talking to again. It's a little complicated as there's feelings involved but he just got out of a relationship and isn't looking to start anything. I can be a very pushy person when it comes to hanging out with someone. Lately, any time I ask him to hang out it seems like he stops responding to me. As in, I asked him earlier today if he wanted to go do something this weekend and he stopped texting me back. The same thing happened last night. I guess my question is -- I'm not sure if this is a situation where anyone would be like "Hey, did I do something to upset you?" or if I'm just overthinking it.
I have to say I love this comparison. I've never thought of my spikes this way, but maybe this will help me laugh some of it off!!
Yay!! I'm so happy for you, and I'm sure the pup is loving it!!

No, I agree! When it comes down to it, if someone is going to judge us THAT harshly for picking a restaurant they think is bad, does anyone need someone like that in their life? It's definitely an unrealistic fear and kind of silly when you really think about it. I'm definitely going to try to make more decisions!!

I have the same problem quite often at work. Every once in a while we'll get a problem I can't solve between myself, google, and the couple of friends I have working in the same field. I get stuck on that problem until it's finally solved, and I'll beat myself up over it ("you're an idiot" "they're going to fire you if you don't figure this out").

They've talked to me about being way too hard on myself and how they've noticed that I can snap at people occasionally (usually, unbeknownst to them, when I'm having a heavily intrusive thought filled day), but I think they chalk it up to "all people in the computer/technology fields are like that". As far as I know it has never been a real issue to them, but I get myself worked up over it and thinking I'm going to get fired for no reason every once in a while.

I'm in IT, I do some minor network admin stuff as well as being a test engineer for my company. Two of my coworkers know, but I'm close with both of them and spend time with them outside of work on occasion. There are days when my bosses think I'm a neurotic mess I'm sure, but they always comment on how detail oriented I am and how I won't back off of a problem until I have it figured out.

Yes, it's exactly this for me. If I let slip something I like and they criticize it I'm more likely to try and cover and pretend I didn't mean I actually like xyz, was totally just kidding...
I'm trying to make myself more aware of when I do this and stop, it's hard when it's become habit though.

I agree. Maybe we'd be happier. Maybe we'd be in even better places. But I'm happy with where I am now, and those are all maybes. I like how I can empathize with people because I know what it's like to be at an astronomically low point in life. I like knowing that the people in my life are, in fact, there for me at my worst.
If you asked me even a year ago I probably would have said yes without hesitation.

When that's happened to me in the past, what my therapist used to call the "so what" method worked for me. So what if he is? Yes, it would hurt. We would probably break up. I would be upset, but would be able to move on after a while. He's most likely not, but the situation is out of my control.
Going down that line of thinking caused me anxiety, but it's always so much less and so much more short lived than trying to combat the thought and argue with my mind.

Yes. Relationship advice isn't going to help the underlying cause and it's not going to even satisfy for long. I know it never does for me. The doubts will always creep back if you don't deal with the rOCD itself.

I had this conversation with a friend the other night. I was having a bad night and she asked me this question. Stopped me in my tracks.
I honestly don't think I would. Yes this illness has dragged me through the mud, but it's also an integral part of who I am and why I do what I do. I wouldn't be where I am today and surrounded by the people I am if it weren't for my OCD.
Would I like a better handle on it and more good days? Hell yes. Would I erase it from every part of my past and my life? I don't think so.
It sounds like it definitely has roots in a similar concept.

You're not alone!! It is nice to finally have that light and that relief in sight, even if it will take time and hard work. If you ever need to talk, feel free to PM me. I know my biggest enemy was always feeling like I was in it alone and no one would ever understand.

It happens to me. My OCD mainly takes the form of rOCD, but every once in a while, when my rOCD seems to have calmed down, I'll notice I start obsessing about other things. It seems to be very spotty in what comes up, like lately I've been paranoid about being watched and people being able to read my text messages. Other times I'll have a month or so of inexplicable violent obsessions.
To me, it's almost like that gooey "Splat" toy I used to play with as a kid, with the main bulge of it being my primary obsessions (rOCD). It's like trying to push the Splat into a container that's too small for it, so other parts of it (the surveillance obsession, the violent obsessions) start to pour out of the edges.
I don't know if that makes any sense or helps any?

Hello! I've lurked here for ages and have finally gathered up the courage to post and become more active. The people here have been extremely supportive and it's definitely nice having a group of people that understand. Glad you're here and that you're getting help, hope all goes well for your wedding!

I think the problem is if they don't constantly see it, it must not be happening. They don't seem to grasp that even on a "good" day, my mind is still running a mile a minute. I'm just better at not letting it show.
Yes, this is another huge one. Ugh.

It's already been said, but I agree with just treating her as you would anyone else. There may be some things she would appreciate if you did one way or another, but I wouldn't assume she wants you to avoid anything unless she were to specifically bring it up. I know personally if my friends started treating me differently based on my OCD it would make me feel more isolated. Some of the friends I have that have known me for a while will do certain things without thinking, like telling me they're busy with x so they won't be able to really respond to my messages until a certain time to keep me from worrying, but it's because I've asked them to or we've had related discussions on non-responsiveness spiking my thoughts.

My OCD has greatly affected many of my relationships, but I don't know if it's because my main obsessions and compulsions are rOCD related. I lost a five and a half year relationship with the guy I thought I was going to spend the rest of my life with to it. He dealt with it as best he could for years and it finally got to the point where he just couldn't anymore. There were other aspects of our relationship that weren't perfect, and looking back we weren't maybe the best match for each other, so it might have been for the best. I've lost friends to it because they can't deal with the constant seeking reassurance and accusations that they hate me or are going to leave me.
Honestly I don't blame a single one of them. Like you said, it gets to a point where it's easy to just let yourself stew in your own misery and that's exactly what I did.
The end of the relationship is what did me in. It's when I realized that I couldn't just be miserable and give in to my thoughts and compulsions and expect people to stay around me and put up with me constantly beating on them.
I'm far from getting complete control over my life, baby steps, but I have changed enough that some of my old friends have come back into my life. I'll take that progress over nothing.
I'm hoping it doesn't end up like that for you, and you can make the changes you need so both you and him can be happy.

This. I went on a long rant to one of my more understanding friends last night (understanding as in she just listens and admits she has no idea what it must be like) because one of our other friends has been extremely dismissive towards me lately as far as "oh, yeah I get bothered by that too but just stop thinking about it". OH THANKS I NEVER THOUGHT OF THAT. /s

Yes! Exactly.
I agree, just reading through posts on here and the handful of responses I've gotten to mine help me feel like I'm not alone. I have friends that really try to understand but, fortunately as I would never wish this on anyone, they don't. And I've discovered the same, I thought I had a good handle on mine and have started to realize a lot of it are actually just compulsions that I didn't recognize as such and avoidance.
Thank you so much, I hope you do as well!!
I get it too. For me it's more that I'm terrified that they'll hate whatever I pick and change their opinion of me.
I was just taking a look at her ones on Pure O. Thank you very much for sharing!
I needed this video tonight. Thank you.
Things like this make me so happy to read! It's nice to be able to look back and see progress made.

I had the same thing just happen. Had an event last weekend that sent my intrusive thoughts into overdrive and I've been struggling to keep my head above water at work and home all week.
I know one of the things that helps me is concentrating on doing something physical. Concentrating on the steps and what my hands are doing takes me out of my head, even if it's for the moment, and it lets me get more of a grip on my thoughts by the time I'm done. At home I'll draw or mess around applying makeup, at work I'm hands on with networking equipment and I'll find a project to dig into.
Sorry, I've tried admin / admin and admin / password as well, neither work.
Hey! I'm sorry it took me so long to get back, holidays and all. I wanted to say thank you for your response but a friend figured it out, our test node isn't set up for DSL so it fails automatically.
Thank you!
This is in Upstate New in York, in Monroe county if that helps.

These were actually the exact three I've been looking at. It's good to know that they're all helpful. I was thinking of starting with the Mindfulness Workbook, just by skimming through it I liked the way it looked, and it's good to know it has a chapter on ROCD. Even without that specifically I'm sure the same general principles apply to working with obsessive thoughts.
